in.other_title: Closed QA without information asymmetry: debate vs direct QA depends on judge strength
in.rationale: Khan et al. note their expertise gap is only access to information, whereas future models may differ in reasoning. Kenton et al. test closed tasks without information asymmetry and report debate beats consultancy but versus direct QA is mixed: GPT-3.5 benefits (p = 0.037), Pro 1.0 shows no difference and Gemma7B and Pro 1.5 do worse; debaters are still RLHF-tuned, so the honesty-propensity part is not addressed.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate's benefit holds when debaters and judge differ in capability rather than information access, for closed QA with LLM judges

text: The authors state that in their setup the difference between strong and weak models is only access to information, whereas future stronger models may differ in reasoning ability or other skills. They also state they evaluate RLHF-fine-tuned models with a propensity for honesty, so it is unclear whether debate will be suitable for deceptive models.
title: Expertise gap is only information access; RLHF debaters have an honesty propensity
